inputs.text: More tenancies mean little when renters are still being forced from their homes. Rising eviction notices, homelessness and emergency accommodation point to a system that protects insecurity rather than people. The six-year lease rules introduced on March 1 should be judged by whether they give renters—especially those most vulnerable to displacement—real security, not by headline figures that make the housing crisis look better than it is.

output.main_topic: Whether six-year lease rules provide renters with real security amid housing insecurity
subtopics: Renters being forced from their homes
Eviction notices, homelessness and emergency accommodation
Limits of headline figures in assessing the housing crisis
